# The cost of a licence for the business that holds it

*Generated by `alicia/scripts/licence_costs.py` on 17 November 2026 from `regulation-register/licence-costs.json`. Phase 8 of the [re-evaluation plan](plan_levers_reevaluation.md) (DECISIONS E-173). Draft: compiled by AI-assisted desk research; not yet checked by a person.*

## What is counted

- **Fees**, quoted from the fee regulations. Where a fee is set in fee units, it is converted at the unit's current value: NT $1.49 from 2026-07-01; QLD $1.133 from 2026-07-01; TAS $1.96 from 2026-07-01.
- **Not verified:** the NT fee unit value ($1.49) is from search results; the official page refused this environment's requests, so its quote could not be checked.
- **Rounding** follows the law: the NT rounds a fee in revenue units down to the dollar (Revenue Units Act 2009 s 3(2)), and Queensland regulations that say so round in tiers (to 5 cents up to $100, 10 cents up to $1,000 and the dollar up to $5,000): `qld-liquor-licence` (Liquor Regulation 2002 (Qld) s 36DA (current)), `qld-motor-dealer-licence` (Motor Dealers and Chattel Auctioneers Regulation 2014 (Qld) s 34A (current)), `qld-security-licence` (Security Providers Regulation 2008 (Qld) s 27A (current)). Other fees in fee units are shown to the cent.
- **Staff time** to apply and to renew, at $91.54 an hour: the Office of Impact Analysis's rate for work time (*Regulatory Burden Measurement Framework*, July 2026, p. 12).
- **Entry** is the fees and time to get the licence. **Renewal** is the fees and time each time it is renewed, and per year divides that by the years between renewals.
- **Regulatory burden** is the framework's own measure, worked out by the calculator in `regulatory-burden-tool/`: the yearly average of the staff time over 10 years. The framework leaves out government fees, which are transfers to government, so fees are shown beside it.
- **Not counted:** training and qualifications, insurance, waiting time, and any effect on the wider economy (out of scope, owner, 16 November 2026).

## Staff time

Assumed: no regulator publishes how long an application or a renewal takes (Service NSW and QBCC pages searched, 16 November 2026). An entry application means gathering identity, qualification and insurance documents, completing the form and, for some licences, attending in person (individual NSW contractor licences are lodged at a Service NSW centre); a renewal is mostly an online payment. Replace with a sourced figure where a regulator publishes one.

| | Low | Central | High |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hours to apply (entry) | 2 | 4 | 8 |
| Hours to renew | 0.5 | 1 | 2 |

## Licences not yet costed

| Licence | Why |
|---|---|
| `nsw-motor-dealer-licence` | Not used: the fees are in fee units indexed each year to the CPI (Motor Dealers and Repairers Regulation 2014 sch 1, under the regulation's own fee unit rules); the only copy here is the corpus copy of January 2023, and the 2026-27 fee unit value was not found in an official source. |
| `nt-security-licence` | Not found: the Private Security Act 1995 regulations could not be found on the NT register under the names tried, and nt.gov.au refuses this environment's requests. |
| `sa-security-licence` | Partly found: the renewal fee for an individual business licence is $870 (sa.gov.au, business licence holders), but the page with the new-licence fee could not be reached. |
| `tas-security-licence` | Only a 2015 copy of the fee schedule could be read (the register refused the current version), so it is not used. |
| `vic-builder-licence` | Blocked: the Building and Plumbing Commission (formerly the VBA) and the Victorian register refuse this environment's requests, and no saved copy of the Building Regulations 2018 fee schedule is here. |
| `vic-liquor-licence` | Blocked: Liquor Control Victoria's site did not answer, and the saved Liquor Control Reform Regulations 2023 are not in this environment. |
| `vic-plumbing-licence` | Blocked, as for the Victorian builder licence (plumbing licences are issued under the Building Act 1993). |
| `vic-security-licence` | Blocked, as for the other Victorian licences. |

Where a renewal fee is "not published", the regulator works the annual fee out for each licensee (from capacity, trading hours and risk); only its entry fees are counted.

## Limits

- **Fees change each year.** Most are indexed; each figure is as at the regulation's current version, or the fee unit value shown.
- **Staff time is assumed**, as no regulator publishes it; the range shows how much it matters.
- **One class of licence each.** The figures are for a small business holding the basic licence; larger businesses and other classes pay more.
- **Not yet on the website.** Showing these costs on the levers page and the Industry lens is the website session's step 8.6.
